full_judgment: 2. The facts leading to the issuance of the Rule, in short, is that the present petitioners as plaintiffs instituted the above mentioned title suit for permanent injunction. The plaintiffs filing a petition for temporary injunction under Order XXXIX, Rules 1 and 2 CPC averred inter-alia that 15.68 acres of land appertains to plot No. 830 of SA khatian no. 199 corresponding to hal plot No. 819 of Bildumiria mouza under Nazirpur Police Station, Pirojpur belonged to Monoranjan, Umesh Chandra, Gonesh Chandra, Sashi Kumar, Krishna Kumar and Sarna Kumar in different shares. Monoranjan being one of the recorded tenant sold 0.75 acres of land by a kabala dated 21-3-1970 to the plaintiff Nos. 1-4 and one Sahabuddin Miah. The said Monoranjan again sold 0.37½ acres of land to the plaintiff Nos. 1-4 and Sahabuddin on 9-10-1973. The plaintiff Nos. 1-4 sold 0.19 acres of land from the land of first kabala dated 21-3-1970 to others. Thus the plaintiff Nos. 1-4 acquired 0.44-3/4 acres of land through the kabala dated 21-3-1970 and 0.30¼ acres of land through the kabala dated 9-10-1973. Thus they acquired in total 0.75 acres of land. The plaintiffs have been possessing the said land by erecting dwelling but and cow shed etcetera thereon. They have also ponds and trees in the suit land. In the recent settlement, the lands have been rightly recorded in the names of the plaintiffs. The defendant No. 1 very recently on 15-10-2009 threatened the plaintiffs with dispossession from the suit land. He has been giving out in the locality that he will enter forcibly into the suit land to erect but to live thereon. Hence the plaintiffs have been constrained to file the prayer for temporary injunction restraining the defendant No. 1 from entering into the suit land.
